clue.text: What's his catch? Little or nothing!

definitions.text: What's his catch? Little or nothing!

parts.note: surface reading: asking what the hidden snag or drawback of some man is
setter's reading: a clumsy fielder catches almost nothing, because the ball slips through his hands

explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' looks like 'snag', as in what's the catch; it is really a catch in cricket or ball games, which a clumsy person drops.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfingers is the jeering name for a clumsy person who keeps dropping things, especially catches.

clue.text: All agreed to arrange a sum with union

indicators.note: to arrange things is to put them into a fresh order, so these letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Members of a trade union all agree to settle on some sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A unanimous decision is one every party has consented to, with no dissenters at all.

clue.text: One left cloakroom for hire

indicators.note: read as 'departed', it says that one thing has gone away from the word that follows

parts.note: cloakroom is a polite British word for a lavatory
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a cloakroom which is available to rent.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of TOILET to leave TO LET; in Britain 'cloakroom' is a genteel name for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A 'To let' sign marks property that is available to rent, i.e. for hire.

clue.text: Destroy epitaph above

parts.note: Rest In Peace, the usual inscription on a gravestone
up means above, and in a down entry this part sits on top

explanation.surface: Someone wants to deface the inscription on a tomb above them.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip up something, such as a contract or letter, is to tear it apart and so ruin it.

clue.text: Pens edict afresh having done a survey

indicators.note: afresh means done over again in a new way, so the letters are laid out once more in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An official rewrites a decree after carrying out a review.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspected means examined or surveyed carefully, so it stands for having done a survey.

clue.text: Pull back with horrible sneer at groundsmen

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for pull from right to left

parts.note: to drag is to pull

indicators.note: something horrible is ugly and twisted, so the next word's letters are mangled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from the nasty sneer of the people who tend the grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners look after the grounds of a property, which is what groundsmen do.

clue.text: Keep quiet during robery and be quick!

parts.note: surface padding: it sets up the robber's order and gives no letters

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a raid is a robbery; the clue misspells robbery as printed
p, piano, is the musical mark for quietly

explanation.surface: A robber's instruction to an accomplice: stay silent while we rob this place and hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep is part of the instruction in the surface, but cryptically it just goes with 'quiet'; the P goes inside RAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid is a synonym of quick, meaning moving at speed.

clue.text: Dance with Scottish cast

parts.note: the Highlands are the mountainous north of Scotland
to fling is to cast or throw

explanation.surface: A dance performed by a Scottish troupe of actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as a group of performers, but here it is the verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highland fling is a lively traditional solo dance from Scotland.

clue.text: They're cultivated by sleeping with spies

parts.note: bedding someone is sleeping with them
a plant is an agent placed secretly in an organisation

explanation.surface: Some people become cultured by having affairs with secret agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' suggests refined people, but it means grown in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedding plants are annuals raised and planted out in garden beds, so they are things that are cultivated.

clue.text: Flustered if a plan goes wrong

indicators.note: when something goes wrong it falls into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone becomes agitated when their scheme fails.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a flap is an informal idiom for being agitated or panicky.

clue.text: Hesitation of police constable struggling with new rules

indicators.note: struggling and new both suggest disorder and a fresh form, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: PC is the standard abbreviation for police constable
taken as written

explanation.surface: A police officer hesitates while trying to get to grips with new regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruple is a moral doubt that makes one hesitate before acting.

clue.text: Crime? Man, it's bad!

parts.note: a man is referred to as he

indicators.note: bad suggests something spoiled or out of order, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in disgust at a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A heist is a robbery, typically an ambitious, planned one, so it is a crime.

clue.text: Before was inclined to have put on an act

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
tended means was inclined to

explanation.surface: Someone who was previously disposed to playact.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to put on an act, faking feelings or behaviour.

clue.text: Tiny pieces of a most unusual design

indicators.note: an unusual design is an odd arrangement, so these letters take a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Small fragments arranged in a most original pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms are the smallest units of matter, hence tiny pieces of anything.

clue.text: Only go so far to give up drink

parts.note: to stop doing something is to give it up
a short is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Advice to someone cutting down on alcohol: limit yourself and quit drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: A short is British pub talk for a measure of spirits, as opposed to a long drink like beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop short is to halt before reaching the end, i.e. to go only part of the way.

clue.text: Generally found underwater

definitions.meaning: first meaning: for the most part, on the whole
second meaning: located in the sea, the main being an old word for the ocean

explanation.walkthrough: The main is a poetic word for the open sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for 'mostly', and read literally it places something out in the open sea.

clue.text: Pointless season sets off concerns

indicators.note: without a point means a compass point letter such as N, S, E or W is dropped from the next word

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of place, so the letters before it are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pointless time of year triggers worries.
explanation.walkthrough: W, for west, is the compass point removed from WINTER to leave INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Interests are matters that involve or affect someone, the same sense as concerns.

clue.text: Airless arena building with old boy in charge

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters of the word before it are put together in a new form

parts.note: taken as written
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A stuffy stadium being constructed, with a former pupil running the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' looks like a noun for the arena, but it is the verb telling you to rebuild its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaerobic means without oxygen, used of processes or organisms needing no air.

clue.text: Girl's wrong — man is out of shape

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, here with the possessive s
a tort is a civil wrong in law
Ed is a short man's name

explanation.surface: A man complains that a girl is wrong about his body being unfit.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a legal term for a wrongful act that leads to civil liability.
explanation.definitionFit: Distorted means twisted or deformed, pulled out of its true shape.

clue.text: The way a politician makes an impression …

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
taken as written
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Describing how a politician manages to win people over, continued in the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp is a mark pressed into a surface, i.e. an impression.

clue.text: … the ultimate politician''s final fatal move

parts.note: ultimate means last
Jack Straw, the British Labour Home and Foreign Secretary

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a politician's ultimate fatal mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was a senior British Labour cabinet minister under Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: The last straw, from the straw that broke the camel's back, is the final addition that causes collapse.

clue.text: Increase desire to go after headship

indicators.note: going after means following, so the wish word is placed behind the other piece

parts.note: read as head of ship, the first letter of ship
an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: Ambition growing in someone keen to pursue a head teacher's post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headship' reads as a head teacher's job, but split it into head of 'ship'.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden powerful rise, so it is an increase.

clue.text: Extend shelter for a women's group

parts.note: the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women
a den is a sheltered lair or hideaway

explanation.surface: Enlarge the refuge used by a women's organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a well-known British organisation for women.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen something is to make it broader, which extends it.

clue.text: Creature hatching from some similar variety

indicators.note: from some says the letters are drawn out of part of the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A creature emerges from an egg of a related kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the young form of an insect that has just hatched from its egg.

clue.text: Breathing space before the final attack

parts.note: a lung is the organ holding the air we breathe

indicators.note: final points to the very end letter of the word just before it

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pause for breath before the decisive assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathing space' seems to mean a rest, but it is the organ of breathing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden thrust forward, as in fencing, i.e. an attack.

clue.text: Worried over changes in student body

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the National Union of Students, the UK student organisation

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Anxiety about reforms in a student union.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous means anxious or uneasy, the same as worried.

clue.text: Idiot ringing over bill

parts.note: the sound a bell makes when ringing

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for bill is read from the end back

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

explanation.surface: A fool keeps ringing up about an unpaid account.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingbat is slang for a stupid or eccentric person.

clue.text: Judge's grave pronouncement

parts.note: surface reading: a judge's solemn, serious statement
setter's reading: grave also means the burial place, so this ruling sends the convict to the grave

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' means serious, and also hints at the burial that follows a capital ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentence of execution is the gravest ruling a judge can hand down.
